entry_state: Loss releases preserve finance and service origins. A holdings change leaves an old OCI schedule frozen at the change-date assumptions, independent of new valuation outcomes. Derecognition now asks which original policy produced the accumulated balance.
exit_state: OCI derecognition follows the balance's origin; mixed-origin early termination remains open. Identical single-date claim distributions can yield different treaty recoveries, so the joint law must be retained rather than inferred from means or independence.
findings: The homogeneous transfer cases have equal cash and equity but different recycling under 88(b) and 89(b). Pending policy-change runoff is explicitly excluded, preserving the open interaction.
The binary joint family has expected recovery 20a, ranging from 0 to 10. Independence gives 5 as one member, and a mean-input calculation gives the wrong zero whenever a is positive.
The conditional transition probabilities 2a and 1 minus 2a reproduce the table without assigning a probability law over the unresolved parameter. No new defect observed.
